Exact worktree search inspects staged/live tracked changes and Git-visible untracked supported text, removes matches for deleted HEAD files, and reports best-effort coverage and provenance. Ignored, binary, unsupported, unreadable, and otherwise excluded files are not silently treated as searched.

For a stale or unindexed HEAD, inspect the reported state and refresh explicitly when appropriate. For an exact-search missing-object error, preserve the reported blob ID; RepoDB does not return a partial result or substitute another object. Unsupported/binary/excluded content and worktree coverage gaps are not evidence that the content was searched.

`--worktree` is opt-in, only with the actual checked-out HEAD as start commit and only when that HEAD is captured in the index. An alternate `--commit` plus `--worktree` fails, as does a stale/missing indexed HEAD; report a machine-readable reason and refresh guidance. The existing `--current-worktree` name continues to mean HEAD-only; never silently change its meaning. HEAD → staged and staged → live worktree are distinct layers; eligible untracked files appear as additions. Discover untracked files as ordinary `git status` would, respecting ignore rules; unsupported/binary/excluded files appear in coverage metadata. No on-disk retained overlay. Best-effort inspection on each search may observe concurrent changes; label time and state/coverage, without claiming an atomic snapshot.

**Current worktree scope**:
A search scope representing the repository's checked-out commit, excluding staged, unstaged, and untracked changes.
_Avoid_: working-tree search (when referring to this narrower scope)

**Verified.** [`src/history.rs::search`](../../src/history.rs) partitions eligible occurrences by `blob_id`, then selects one with `ORDER BY timestamp DESC, o.commit_id DESC, path ASC`; filtering occurs first. The chosen occurrence's segmentation kind selects its units. The [`README.md`, “References, duplicates, and ordering”](../../README.md) warns this is committer-time policy, **not ancestry ordering**, and identical unit text in distinct blobs is not collapsed. **Impact (inference):** an all-history answer may attribute old text to a later copy, a timestamp-skewed commit, or another path; a file moved or represented as both docs/source may return only one path and one segmentation. A single-commit scope is an effective existing workaround, while all-history is not an occurrence timeline.

Commit filtering happens **before** ordinary-search duplicate collapse. Each
indexed unit of an identical blob appears once, at the newest eligible occurrence:
committer timestamp descending, then full commit ID descending, then path ascending
(byte order). `--explore` bypasses this collapse and pages every eligible
commit/path reference.
This is a deterministic timestamp policy, not ancestry ordering. The chosen
occurrence's path determines the segmentation kind; only that representation of
the blob is returned, even when identical content occurs as both `.md` and `.rs`.
Excluding the chosen commit can reveal an older occurrence and its segmentation.
Different blobs, or distinct units within one blob, are not collapsed merely
because their text is equal.

If a complete result cannot fit, RepoDB emits its reference and sets
`text_omitted_for_size` rather than cutting text. Fetch that result separately
by repeating the same search with `--fetch-reference REFERENCE_ID`; increase
`--byte-budget` enough to fit the complete result. `--fetch-reference` cannot be
combined with `--explore` or `--cursor`. If even the minimal reference cannot
fit, search returns an explicit `result_limit` error. `--explore` removes text
recursively, including indexed/live semantic text, but preserves references and
ranking/provenance metadata.

Imports are explicit and single-source: a URL import fetches only that page and
never crawls linked pages. Search never fetches or refreshes; refreshing
registered URLs is explicit. See `repodb import --help` and `repodb refresh --help`.

SOURCE is one local file, one HTTP(S) page URL, or one Git repository. A URL
import fetches only the selected page; it does not crawl links. Search never
fetches. `repodb refresh` or `repodb refresh --imports` explicitly refreshes
registered URLs and other imports.

If both are available, explain that indexed results can be stale after repository changes. Suggest `repodb refresh` when relevant, but do not refresh automatically. Availability does not establish freshness or semantic-search readiness.
An initialized database can be stale. Search does not refresh it. Suggest an explicit `repodb refresh` if relevant, but do not refresh automatically.

- **Proton requirement:** Automated traffic must remain consistent with normal client behavior and must not resume in a burst after service failures or restart.
- **Primary source:** Mutable — Title: Proton Terms of Service; Publisher: Proton AG; URL: https://proton.me/legal/terms; Accessed: 2026-10-02.
- **Project interpretation:** Direct and SDK rate limits establish one durable account-independent deadline shared by gateway and monitor instances. Restart cannot shorten it; expiry admits one probe, repeated throttling extends it, and success clears only the observed generation.
- **Status:** `compliant-automatic`
- **Summary:** `compliant`
- **Implementation evidence:** [durable Proton throttle](https://github.com/emfrom/protonsync/blob/d99ca89d6179cd9efa6f9586d7d9551a6e5f4064/src/proton-throttle.ts) and [gateway integration](https://github.com/emfrom/protonsync/blob/d99ca89d6179cd9efa6f9586d7d9551a6e5f4064/src/proton-gateway.ts).
- **Automatic test evidence:** [`an expired cooldown admits one probe and renewed throttling extends it without a queued burst`](https://github.com/emfrom/protonsync/blob/d99ca89d6179cd9efa6f9586d7d9551a6e5f4064/test/proton-throttle.test.js), restart and generation-race cases in that file, and the SDK cooldown case in `test/proton-gateway.test.js` at the same commit.
- **Manual evidence:** Not required — reconstructed instances over temporary durable state prove restart behavior.
- **Revalidation trigger:** Throttle persistence, gateway/monitor construction, probe admission, SDK error mapping, status output, or service restart changes.

The SDK request contract carries `timeoutMs`; the installed SDK sets 30 seconds for metadata and 600 seconds for storage (`node_modules/@protontech/drive-sdk/src/internal/apiService/apiService.ts:185-193`, `:241-253`). protonsync's adapter type omits `timeoutMs` and passes only the SDK signal into `fetch` (`src/proton-gateway.ts:213-235`). If the SDK does not separately abort that signal, the documented timeout is ineffective.

`protonsync status` classifies the relationship as `synchronized`, `active`, `degraded`, `blocked`, or `repair-required`. It also reports the last successful activity, cursor state, pending work, retries, permanent failures, and unresolved conflicts. JSON status contains the same health summary for scripts.

```bash
protonsync --help
protonsync --version
protonsync config show
```
Proton’s SDK documentation says:

```bash
protonsync config show
protonsync config show --json
protonsync config show --direction upload-only
protonsync config show --propagate-deletions
```

**Assessment:** confirmed compatibility gap. It directly explains why a recoverable Proton challenge cannot be completed in protonsync. Confirm whether this is the observed path by capturing the response code and non-secret verification method names.

`protonsync status` classifies the relationship as `synchronized`, `active`, `degraded`, `blocked`, or `repair-required`. It also reports the last successful activity, cursor state, pending work, retries, permanent failures, and unresolved conflicts. JSON status contains the same health summary for scripts.

```bash
protonsync --help
protonsync --version
protonsync config show
```
Proton’s SDK documentation says:

```bash
protonsync config show
protonsync config show --json
protonsync config show --direction upload-only
protonsync config show --propagate-deletions
```

**Assessment:** confirmed compatibility gap. It directly explains why a recoverable Proton challenge cannot be completed in protonsync. Confirm whether this is the observed path by capturing the response code and non-secret verification method names.
